name: Shaidan Shaari Bin Abd Rasep
role: Infrastructure & Security Engineer turned AI Systems Builder
summary: I started in the server room. Ten-plus years ago that was AIX boxes, Cisco switches and VLANs at IBM Malaysia: 50+ servers, 99.9% uptime, and the humility that comes from being on call when a box stops answering. Then a co-founded e-commerce business doing RM 500K a year, where the same discipline met marketing budgets and 4:1 ad ROI.

Now I build AI systems and still operate the infrastructure underneath them. That is the part most AI work skips. A decade accountable for uptime changes how you build: you think about blast radius, rollback strategy, and why an approval gate exists before the automation does something you cannot undo.

capabilities.title: AI systems that ship
capabilities.body: Multi-agent orchestration, LLM routing with failover, approval gates, human-in-the-loop UX. The fleet that runs NusaByte is 19 specialists with scopes, not one general assistant — a mis-route is visible instead of silently wrong.

capabilities.title: Automation that holds
capabilities.body: Workflows with a deterministic fallback when the model is unavailable, and an audit trail of who approved what. Record-then-send, so a transport outage can never destroy an operator's work.

capabilities.title: Infrastructure I maintain
capabilities.body: Linux, Docker, systemd, PM2, Traefik, PostgreSQL, canary deploys with automated rollback. I still own the servers the agents run on, which is why the agents are boring in the ways that matter.

capabilities.title: Security as a default
capabilities.body: Certified Ethical Hacker. Wazuh SIEM, OSSEC, WAF on the OWASP Top 10 rule set, full mail authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC), scoped service keys so machine callers never hold admin credentials.

systems.name: JEBAT CENTRIX
systems.problem: Inbound enquiries needed triage, quoting, and assignment across a team, done manually and inconsistently.
systems.approach: Nineteen specialists behind one natural-language front door rather than one general assistant. Each agent has a scope, so a mis-route is visible instead of silently wrong. Rejected a single mega-prompt — it had no way to express "this question is outside what I know."
systems.shipped: Live. Natural-language routing, parallel fan-out across independent workstreams, weighted dispatch, per-call cost and usage instrumentation, and mandatory approval on anything outbound or destructive.
systems.broke: A bot token was revoked and polling died with an error that named no cause — "no adapter available". The real fault was a plugin timeout of 10 seconds against a provider that needed longer to warm up. Raised it to 120 and documented why, because the fast default was only ever fast for local responses. Provider 429s under repeated load now degrade with an explicit retry message rather than a confident wrong answer.

systems.name: WhatsApp sales desk
systems.problem: Enquiries arrived by WhatsApp with no consistent triage, and quotations lived in someone's head.
systems.approach: Inbound → intent, entity and urgency triage → auto-drafted quotation written into a live ledger → weighted round-robin dispatch. Two decisions worth defending: triage is model-assisted but has a deterministic rule fallback, so it degrades instead of failing; and replies are recorded before delivery is attempted, so a gateway outage can never destroy an operator's work.
systems.shipped: Live with approval gating. Transport is pluggable — official Cloud API or a self-hosted gateway — behind one interface, so the channel can change without touching business logic.
systems.broke: Triage failed silently for a while. Duplicate config lines had concatenated two valid keys into one invalid 112-character string, and the configured model had been retired from the provider. The 404 said nothing about the key.

systems.name: Search-readiness engine
systems.problem: Clients had no defensible way to know whether their site would survive an AI-answer-engine world, and no route from a diagnosis to paid work.
systems.approach: Score a site across ten dimensions — technical SEO, E-E-A-T signals, AI-answer-engine readiness, structured data, programmatic SEO — then turn the score into a priced, phased scope routed to the agent that owns each workstream. Free scan in, priced scope out.
systems.shipped: 1,200+ line engine, live. Drove one client's E-E-A-T score 66 → 100, AI-SEO 90 → 100, GEO 31 → 80, overall 87 → 98.
systems.broke: Found a class of production defect where the build shipped stale prerendered pages — source right, production wrong, and nothing in the pipeline capable of saying so. Fixed at the source: the build now deletes its own output first, and -SkipBuild warns when packaged prerenders predate the source they came from. Also found `npm run build` had never worked inside the deploy script — npm's PowerShell shim dies in that context, so every "successful" deploy had quietly avoided it.

systems.name: Einaq Baby Carrier
systems.problem: A physical product business with no digital channel and a marketing budget that had to justify itself monthly.
systems.approach: Built and ran the whole platform: storefront, payments, production workflow, paid acquisition, and the reporting that told us which of those were working.
systems.shipped: RM 500K+ annual revenue within two years, 4:1 ad ROI, 80% of sales through digital marketing, 25% material waste reduction and RM 50K annual cost cuts from workflow changes.
systems.broke: Cloud-based server monitoring on AWS EC2 replaced guessing about whether the store was up — it eliminated the bulk of the downtime we'd previously only learned about from customers.
